title: Mandatory short-term rental accommodation register (WA)
summary: Under the Short-Term Rental Accommodation Act 2024, WA opened a statewide STRA register on 1 July 2024 and made registration mandatory from 1 January 2025, with registration numbers required on advertisements and planning approvals phased in by 2026.
direction_rationale: Registration, night caps and levies raise costs or limit supply for short-term rental hosts, reducing competition faced by hotels and other accommodation providers.
comparison: States without registration (QLD, SA); NSW (registered since 2021)
confounders: local council caps (e.g. Byron Shire 60 days)
notes: WA also offered incentives to convert STRA to long-term rentals.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use. Primary commencement chosen on 15 October 2026 as the date the change described in the title took effect; confirm on review.

assessment.summary: A mandatory statewide register for short-term rentals, with planning approvals phased in. It adds costs and conditions for hosts; effects on long-term rental supply are not weighed here.

marks.reason: Hosts must register and show registration numbers on every listing.
Phased-in planning approvals add a condition for new unhosted short-term rentals.
